validation.title: Automatic validations
validation.lead: On submission: healthcheck of the service through the gateway and contract test (Schemathesis) against the sandbox. The operator approves only if they passed.
validation.rerunHint: Did you fix the service? Run the validations again.

rootAnswered.meaning: The service answered HTTP {http} at its root. That is fine: any answer that is not a 5xx proves the gateway reaches the service, and many services have nothing at their root.

unreachableNode.meaning: HTTP {http} comes from the gateway, not from the service: it could not reach the entity's node, or the node did not answer in time. Usually the node is off, its tunnel is down, or the service is not running on the node.
unreachableNode.next: Check the node's status and last heartbeat (above, and in My entity → Kit nodes), that its tunnel is up on the entity's server, and that the service runs on the node at this service path. Then run the validations again.

unreachableDirect.meaning: HTTP {http} comes from the gateway, not from the service: it could not reach the service's URL, or the service did not answer in time (DNS, firewall or TLS certificate).
unreachableDirect.next: Check that the URL answers from outside the entity's network, that its firewall lets the gateway in, and its TLS certificate. Then run the validations again.

unreachableXroad.meaning: HTTP {http} comes from the gateway, not from the service: it got no answer through the X-Road Security Server.
unreachableXroad.next: Check the operator's Security Server, and that the service is registered in X-Road and allowed for the network's client. Then run the validations again.

serviceError.meaning: The gateway reached the service, but the service answered HTTP {http} at its root: it is running and failing.
serviceError.next: Check the service's logs. Its root only needs to answer without a 5xx: a 404 is fine. Then run the validations again.

timeout.meaning: The gateway did not answer within 15 seconds: the service is very slow or the connection to it hangs.
timeout.next: Check that the service (or the node and its tunnel) answers quickly. Then run the validations again.

gatewayDown.meaning: The portal could not reach the gateway. This is a problem of the platform, not of the service.
gatewayDown.next: The operator checks that the gateway (APISIX) is running and reachable from the portal's API. Then run the validations again.

noRoute.meaning: The gateway did not receive the verification route of this version in time.
noRoute.next: The operator looks for errors on this version in the gateway sync console. Then run the validations again.

notConfigured.meaning: This deployment has no validation token (DEN_VALIDATION_TOKEN), so the healthcheck cannot run.
notConfigured.next: The operator sets it in the deployment and restarts the API. Then run the validations again.

unknown.meaning: The healthcheck failed for a reason the portal does not recognize.
unknown.next: Run the validations again. If it keeps failing, the operator checks the API's logs.

mismatch.meaning: The sandbox answered differently from what the OpenAPI declares in {count, plural, one {this operation} other {these operations}}: {operations}.
mismatch.next: Fix the sandbox service so that it answers as the OpenAPI declares. If the document is the one that is wrong, the operator requests changes and the provider uploads a corrected one. Then run the validations again.

runnerDown.meaning: The contract-test service (contract-runner) did not answer. This is a problem of the platform, not of the service.
runnerDown.next: The operator checks the contract-runner service. Then run the validations again.

timeout.meaning: The contract test took longer than allowed: the sandbox answers too slowly or not at all.
timeout.next: Check that the sandbox (its node and tunnel, or its URL) answers quickly. Then run the validations again.

couldNotStart.meaning: Schemathesis could not start testing: usually the sandbox is not reachable through the gateway, or requests cannot be generated from the OpenAPI.
couldNotStart.next: Check the sandbox (its node and tunnel, or its URL) and the operations of the OpenAPI document. Then run the validations again.

noOperations.meaning: The OpenAPI declares no operation the contract test could call.
noOperations.next: Check the document's paths and operations. Then run the validations again.

noSandbox.meaning: The version declares no sandbox, so the contract test did not run. This does not block the approval.

runnerNotConfigured.meaning: This deployment has no contract-test service, so the test did not run. This does not block the approval.

unknown.meaning: The contract test failed for a reason the portal does not recognize.
unknown.next: Run the validations again. If it keeps failing, the operator checks the API's logs.

operation.serverError: the sandbox answered a server error
operation.mismatch: the answer does not match the OpenAPI (status code, content type or response schema)

secret.title: Save the secret now
secret.warning: This secret is shown only once. Copy it and keep it somewhere safe: the portal does not store it and you will not be able to see it again.

detail.pendingNote: We are creating the credentials in the identity server. This takes a few seconds.
detail.guideNote: Set DEN_CLIENT_SECRET to the secret you kept when you created the application. You need an approved access request for the gateway to accept the call.
detail.guideLimit: Each subscription has a limit of requests per minute. Over it, the gateway answers 429 in application/problem+json (code rate_limited); the X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset headers give the limit, what is left and in how many seconds it resets.
detail.guideEndUser: X-DEN-End-User identifies the official making the request. It is required by APIs with personal or sensitive data: 1 to 128 visible characters, no spaces (for example, their user name or work e-mail). The gateway turns it into a hash with the network’s salt: neither the provider nor the logs see the value.
detail.guideMtls: The network requires mTLS: both calls present the application's certificate (Client certificate section) and its private key. The token is bound to that certificate and only works with it. The gateway's certificate is issued by the network's certificate authority:

certificates.title: Client certificate (mTLS)
certificates.required: The network requires mTLS: the gateway only accepts calls from this application with a valid certificate issued by the network.
certificates.optional: For now the certificate is optional on this network. Once mTLS is required, the gateway will only accept calls with a valid certificate issued by the network.
certificates.howTo: 1. On your application's server, generate the private key and the certificate signing request (CSR). The private key never leaves that server:
certificates.paste: 2. Paste the content of the .csr file here. The portal has it signed by the network's certificate authority.
certificates.csrHint: In PEM format: it starts with -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE REQUEST-----. It must name this application only (CN = its client ID).
certificates.issued: The certificate is ready. Download it and install it on your server next to the private key.
certificates.conflict: The application already has a valid certificate, or it is not active.
certificates.inactive: Only an active application can get a certificate.
certificates.readOnly: Only members with the developer role can request certificates.
certificates.unavailable: The certificate authority is not available right now. Try again in a few minutes.

errors.malformed: This is not a certificate signing request (CSR) in PEM format.
errors.signature: The CSR signature is not valid: generate it again.
errors.subject: The CSR must name this application only: CN equal to its client ID and no other name.
errors.key: The key must be ECDSA P-256 or P-384, or RSA of 2048 to 4096 bits.

certificates.renewHint: You can request a new certificate to renew it: the current one keeps working for {days, plural, one {# more day} other {# more days}}.
certificates.rotationInProgress: A certificate renewal is in progress: revoke the previous one once you no longer use it, or wait for its period to end.

rotation.rotateSecretHint: Generates a new secret. The current one keeps working for {days, plural, one {# more day} other {# more days}}, so you can switch your system without downtime.
rotation.newSecretWarning: This secret is shown only once: copy it and keep it somewhere safe. The previous one keeps working until {date}; revoke it once your system uses the new one.
rotation.secretInProgress: A secret rotation is in progress. Revoke the previous secret once you no longer use it, or wait for its period to end.
rotation.revokeWarning: It stops working at once and cannot be undone.
rotation.revokeReason: Reason (optional, kept in the audit trail)
rotation.conflict: The credential changed meanwhile or this operation is not possible. Reload the page.

guide.lead: A complete program in each language: it gets the token and calls an API with the DEN headers. The secret is read from the DEN_CLIENT_SECRET environment variable, never from the code. Replace the path, the purpose and the official with those of your approved request.

nodeContract.title: Contract the node serves
nodeContract.lead: In every heartbeat the node reports the SHA-256 of each service’s OpenAPI; it is compared with the published version’s. It never blocks traffic: the gateway keeps routing by the published contract.
nodeContract.consoleTitle: Nodes not serving the published contract
nodeContract.consoleLead: Published versions whose node serves an OpenAPI other than the published one, or reports none. Traffic keeps flowing; the entity decides whether to publish a new version or go back to the published contract.
nodeContract.matches: The node serves the published OpenAPI on {path}.
nodeContract.differs: The node serves an OpenAPI other than the published one on {path}.
nodeContract.differsNext: Traffic keeps flowing with the published contract. If the change is deliberate, publish a revision or a new version with the OpenAPI the node serves; if not, put the published OpenAPI back on the node.
nodeContract.notReportedNoOpenapi: The node’s service {service} does not report its OpenAPI, so it cannot be compared with the published one (the node’s logs show its routes as “(unknown)”). For an entity’s own API behind the node, set the OpenAPI file in the service’s “openapi” and restart the node; for an instant API, check that the service starts.
nodeContract.notReportedNoService: The node declares no service on {path}. Check the version’s service path and the node’s configuration.

certificateRevocations.title: Mass certificate revocation
certificateRevocations.lead: Revoke at once the live client certificates that match the filters, in an incident: a compromised entity, a batch issued with a flaw, or the intermediate CA. Each one stops working at the gateway with the next OPA bundle (under 60 seconds), and the developers of each application are told to issue a new one. The full procedure is in the operator runbook.

filters.title: Which certificates
filters.hint: All filters apply together. Dates are of issuance, in UTC. Without filters, every live certificate of the network.
filters.issuerSelected: Only those issued by the intermediate

preview.title: What would be revoked
preview.empty: No live certificate matches these filters.
preview.count: {count, plural, one {# certificate} other {# certificates}} of {entities, plural, one {# entity} other {# entities}}
preview.wholeNetwork: No filters: every live certificate of the network would be revoked. Use it only if the intermediate CA is compromised.

issuers.title: Intermediate CAs that issued them
issuers.hint: To revoke only what one intermediate issued (for instance, the previous one after a rotation).
issuers.subject: Intermediate

certificateRevocations.revokeHint: It cannot be undone: each application will have to issue a new certificate. If someone issues or revokes a certificate meanwhile, nothing is revoked and the list must be seen again.
certificateRevocations.reasonHint: It goes to the audit trail of each certificate. At least 10 characters; no personal data.

kit.title: The node kit
kit.publicLead: Provider entities connect their services to the network through the node: software installed on one of the entity's servers, which opens an encrypted tunnel outward. This is the version the operator offers now.
kit.publicToken: Installing it takes an enrollment token, which the entity's administrator issues in the portal (My entity → Kit nodes → Register a node) once the entity is part of the network. An entity that is not part of it yet signs in and asks to join first.
kit.sectionLead: Download it on the server where the node will run. The enrollment token comes from "Register a node".
kit.none: The operator has not published a version of the kit yet.
kit.checksumIsConvenience: The checksum on this page is a convenience, not a guarantee: whoever controls the portal controls both the file and its checksum.
kit.unsignedCheck: This release is not signed yet. Before installing, compare the checksum with the one the operator gives you through another channel (for example, the agreement with your entity).
kit.signedCheck: The guarantee is the operator's signature: check it with the operator's key as you received it through another channel (for example, the agreement with your entity), not with the one shown here.
kit.commandsLead: On the entity's server (Ubuntu Server 22.04 or 24.04), as a user with sudo. The second command must say "OK"; if it does not, do not open the bundle.
kit.commandsFromPortal: Commands, downloading from this portal's mirror
kit.portalAnswer: When the installer asks for the portal URL, answer <url></url>; then paste the enrollment token when it asks for it.
kit.afterInstall: The installer ends with "The node is online", and the node shows as Online on the Kit nodes page. The kit's own guide is inside the bundle (INSTALL.md).

kitAdmin.title: Node kit
kitAdmin.lead: The kit version entities see on their Kit nodes page and on the public site. The kit is released in its own repository: here you say which version is current, its link and its checksum, and you can mirror its bundle on this portal for servers that cannot reach the release.
kitAdmin.mirroredLocked: Mirrored: its file, size and checksum no longer change.

form.title: Set the current version
form.lead: Copy the link, the size and the SHA-256 from the kit's release (its ".sha256" file). Saving makes it the current version at once; an existing version is corrected.
form.label: Set the current version of the kit
form.url: Link to the bundle (https, ending in .tar.gz)
form.signatureUrl: Link to the signature (optional, once releases are signed)
form.saved: Saved: it is the current version.

upload.hint: It must have exactly {bytes} bytes and the SHA-256 of the release; it cannot be replaced afterwards.
